factors.name: Connectivity and branching
factors.summary: Very high loadings (0.86–0.97) of average and maximum connector degree, token split, arcs per node and control flow complexity, joined by empty sequence flows (0.75) and connector mismatch (0.56). The factor captures how many arcs attach to connectors and splits, that is, how densely branched and interconnected a net is. It carries 50% of the variance and dominates the solution, and Size also loads moderately on it (0.45).

factors.name: Size and non-separability
factors.summary: Size (0.85) and Separability (0.82) load highly, with a secondary loading of Sequentiality (0.50). In this dataset, larger nets tend to have a higher share of nodes that are not articulation points. The factor rests on only two clearly assigned measures, and Size also loads 0.45 on Factor 1.

factors.name: Sequentiality and connector-type mix
factors.summary: Sequentiality (0.79) and Connector Heterogeneity (0.66) load positively, with a weaker loading of Number of empty sequence flows (0.43). Why a high share of non-connector arcs should go together with a mix of parallel and choice connectors is not obvious from the definitions. Connector Heterogeneity is also undefined for nets without connectors and has a low communality (0.46), so this factor is tentative.

factors.name: Weak residual factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor, which explains only 2.6% of the variance (SS loadings 0.29). Its largest loading is Connector Mismatch at 0.38, which stays unassigned here because its main loading on Factor 1 is 0.18 higher, beyond the 0.15 gap; Maximum connector degree follows at 0.28. The factor should not be given a substantive interpretation.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for a factor analysis: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.81. The four varimax factors explain 86% of the variance, but the eigenvalues (7.40, 1.47, 0.96, 0.52) point to two factors, which matches the suggested count. One large connectivity and branching factor dominates, followed by a size and separability factor. Factor 3 is moderately strong but hard to interpret, and Factor 4 is essentially empty. Density was removed by the MSA filter, and Number of duplicate tasks was dropped as constant.
caveats: Four factors were extracted although two were suggested, and Factors 3 and 4 have eigenvalues below 1, so they may reflect over-extraction.
Coefficient of network connectivity has a communality at the bound of the fit (possible Heywood case), so its loading of 0.95 may be inflated.
Density (MSA 0.44) and Number of duplicate tasks (constant) are not part of the solution, so the factors say nothing about them.
Connector Heterogeneity is undefined for nets without connectors, and the handling of these cases may affect its loading on Factor 3.

Several measures have notable secondary loadings that the 0.15-gap rule does not flag as cross-loadings: Size 0.45 on Factor 1, Sequentiality 0.50 on Factor 2 and Number of empty sequence flows 0.43 on Factor 3.
Separability has the lowest MSA (0.61), close to the 0.6 threshold.
The factors describe shared variance among 288 mostly discovered nets under varimax rotation; they depend on this dataset and on the chosen number of factors, and they do not imply causes.
